newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says no date set for crash compensation.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says no date set for crash compensation.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Airlines has not set a date for paying compensation to the families of the victims of the world's deadliest mid-air collision over India, its director-general was on Thursday quoted as saying.

Khaled Ben-Bakr told al-Eqtisadiah newspaper that "the issue of insurance or compensation needs extensive study with several parties including insurance companies and legal authorities, so the issue could not be decided quickly".

Early this week, search teams pulled from the wreckage the last of the bodies of the 349 people aboard the Saudi Arabian Airlines jumbo jet and the Kazakh cargo plane that collided in the sky near Delhi on November 12. There were 312 people on board the Saudi plane.
A New Delhi High Court judge probing the crash has been given until February 15 to complete his inquiry.
